claims.text: Core product is wheat udon made in-house and tempura fried in shared oil; no gluten-free accommodation is documented.
Bukkake and dipping styles use soy-based sauces/broths, which conventionally contain wheat; no wheat-free sauce is documented.
Broths rely on fish/meat dashi (the curry udon uses beef-tendon stock), so no separated vegan preparation is documented.
All core dishes (okonomiyaki, negi-yaki, yakisoba, teppanyaki) are wheat-flour batter or wheat noodles cooked on a shared griddle, with no gluten-free menu or separate preparation.
Dishes are finished with Worcestershire-style okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-based; no gluten-free sauce is offered.
Standard ingredients across the menu include squid, shrimp, beef, fish cake and egg, with bonito/fish dashi in the batter; no vegan separation exists.
All tempura is battered in wheat flour and deep-fried in a shared fryer; no gluten-free option is documented.
Seafood and vegetables are fried in the same oil, and the set includes seafood and miso soup, so vegetable pieces are not separated for vegan diners.
As a traditional Japanese kappo/kaiseki kitchen, dishes rely on dashi and standard Japanese seasonings, which typically include wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
Courses are centered on fish, cod milt, Yamato beef, and venison alongside fish/kombu dashi, so vegan diners cannot avoid animal products in the omakase format.
A flour-based patisserie where wheat is used throughout the cake and pastry production; no separation or gluten-free handling is documented.
Menu is built on dairy, eggs, butter and cream; no plant-based preparation is documented.

name: 菓匠 千壽庵吉宗 奈良総本店 (Kashō Senjuan Yoshimune Nara Sōhonten)

claims.text: The shop is a general wagashi confectionery that also sells wheat-containing sweets; no gluten-free production line or cross-contamination policy is published, so shared utensils/surfaces are likely.
No published allergen or staff allergy-handling protocol; commentary on warabimochi allergens recommends contacting the maker directly to confirm ingredients.

The premium warabimochi is made from only domestic bracken starch, sugar, and water — no additives — and the core warabimochi recipe contains no wheat, making it a relatively simple, plant-based sweet (note the kinako topping is soy).

name: キナリ ピッツァ (Kinari Pizza)

claims.text: All pizzas are baked from wheat dough in a single shared wood-fired oven, so flour cross-contamination is unavoidable; no gluten-free options are documented.
Most pizzas include fresh mozzarella and Grana Padano cheese, and the kitchen also handles Yamato pork, so vegetable pizzas share equipment with dairy and meat.
Heavily vegetable-focused menu using produce from the owner's own farm; the Pizza Ortolana Bianca features around ten kinds of Nara vegetables.
Not a gluten-free kitchen; standard ramen and udon use wheat noodles and soy-based seasonings are used throughout, so the regular menu is not celiac-safe without arrangement.
Soy-based seasonings and soy-meat analogues are central to the menu; assume standard soy sauce contains wheat unless confirmed otherwise.
The kitchen states its cookware and tableware have never been used to cook meat or fish, minimizing animal cross-contact.
Broth uses only kombu and shiitake with no bonito, and dishes are dairy-free and egg-free.
Gluten-free, vegan, and allergy accommodations can be arranged with advance reservation; the owner himself has lifelong allergies and screens ingredients carefully.
Fully 100% plant-based with no animal protein in any ingredient, oil, or broth, plus avoidance of the five pungent vegetables.
English-speaking owner and multilingual support make it easy to discuss dietary needs.
